explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/985: for every prime p, is there a prime q < p that is a primitive root mod p? The statement asserts this for primes p ≠ 2, using orderOf (q : ZMod p) = p - 1. Excluding p = 2 is necessary and correct, since no prime q < 2 exists, so the literal statement fails trivially there. The open tag follows the page, which records no resolution. Faithful.
